items.title: Antonelli arrives as champion; Mercedes targets the constructors' title
items.summary: Antonelli clinched the Drivers' Championship in Mexico and arrives on 380 points, 119 clear of Verstappen. Mercedes leads Ferrari 630–504. Formula1.com's pre-weekend scenario says gaining three points on Ferrari in Brazil seals the constructors' title.
items.why_it_matters: The drivers' title is settled, but the constructors' title is not yet won. These are entering-Brazil totals, not projected race results.

items.title: Russell's reported ICE penalty meets the FIA's season-to-date usage report
items.summary: The Race reports that Mercedes selected Brazil for a new internal-combustion engine and a five-place grid drop. In its 6 November pre-FP1 report, the FIA lists five ICEs, five TCs, five EXHs, four MGU-Ks, four ESs, four PU-CEs and five PU-ANCs used by Russell this season. The usage snapshot is not the event's new-parts declaration or a penalty ruling.
items.why_it_matters: Keep Russell's reported penalty separate from the FIA's season-to-date usage totals; neither document establishes that the planned ADUO engine specification is arriving.

items.title: Six rookies take FP1 seats; Camara makes his Haas race debut
items.summary: Formula1.com lists Fornaroli for Piastri, Beganovic for Leclerc, Browning for Sainz, Slater for Hulkenberg, Mini for Gasly and Herta for Perez in FP1. Herta needs at least 100 km in a clean session for his final Super Licence point. Separately, Camara partners Bearman for the full weekend in place of Ocon; Haas has confirmed the Brazil drive only.
items.why_it_matters: Distinguish six one-session substitutions from Camara's full-weekend F1 debut and from unconfirmed future race seats. Herta's mileage target is a requirement, not a completed result.

items.title: Hamilton set for 400th start as Ferrari talks remain pending
items.summary: Hamilton is set to make his 400th Grand Prix start in Sao Paulo, becoming only the second driver to reach the milestone. On Thursday he said his planned post-Mexico face-to-face discussion with Leclerc had not happened and he wants a stronger working basis for the coming campaign.
items.why_it_matters: The race-week milestone is distinct from the still-pending Ferrari conversation; do not imply that talks occurred or team orders changed.

items.title: FIA Document 12 lists four McLaren updates and ten nil returns
items.summary: FIA Document 12 lists four McLaren performance items: front wing, rear wing, beam wing and floor furniture. The stated aims are flow conditioning or local aerodynamic load. Mercedes, Red Bull, Ferrari, Williams, Racing Bulls, Aston Martin, Haas, Audi, Alpine and Cadillac each return no updates. The Race reports that McLaren's front-wing concept is intended to carry into its 2027 launch specification.
items.why_it_matters: The declaration records team explanations, not independently measured downforce, lap-time or net-performance gains. It also supersedes the earlier pre-publication listing checks; those checks did not establish non-publication.
